title: Failure-path tests that prove the rollback and catch leaks
problem: app.py sends a message as one unit of work: the message row, the chat's message_count and an audit entry are committed together. It's correct. Write four tests in test_failures.py that prove it: the normal path, a duplicate client_id (409), an audit-log outage (503 with nothing saved) and a leak check. test_meta.py runs your tests against five broken copies of app.py.
requirements: Edit only test_failures.py. Don't change app.py, conftest.py or test_meta.py
Keep the four test names. Tests may use the fixtures client, db, engine and connections
Check database state through db (a separate session), not through the response alone
Simulate the audit outage with app.dependency_overrides on client.app, not by editing app.py
All your tests pass on the real app.py
Write the tests from the docstrings and app.py first. Read the mutants only after your first run
contract: test_failures.py defines test_send_saves_message_count_and_audit, test_duplicate_client_id_is_409_and_changes_nothing, test_audit_failure_rolls_back_everything and test_no_connection_is_held_after_requests
expectedBehavior: pytest -q shows your four tests and all five test_tests_kill[...] cases passing
edgeCases: A failure after the first write of the unit of work
A unique-constraint violation detected only at commit
Requests that end in 404 or 409, not just successful ones, for the leak check
Objects cached in the db session hiding what is really in the database
hints: Conceptual: 'nothing was saved' can only be shown by reading the database after the request, through a different session from the app's. Count every table the unit of work touches, plus message_count, before and after.

Specific: write a small helper that returns the message count, the audit count and chat 1's message_count from db. Call db.expire_all() at its start so the session doesn't answer from cached objects. For the outage, make a class whose record() raises AuditUnavailable and put it in client.app.dependency_overrides[get_audit]: FastAPI calls the override, and calling a class makes an instance.

Implementation: the duplicate test sends the same client_id twice, takes the snapshot after the first request, and asserts 409 and an unchanged snapshot after the second. The leak test sends a valid message, one to chat 99 (404) and a duplicate (409), then asserts connections.checkouts > 0 and connections.checked_out() == 0.
evaluation: Every failure-path test asserts the status AND the database state
The outage is simulated with a dependency override
You can say which test kills each mutant, and why commit_after_yield is only visible on the duplicate path
